phase6CrashRestartPath.verdict: PASS — 7 phases, 4 sidecar generations in one session, 0 orphans
phase6CrashRestartPath.whatItClosed: The last thing the keepalive work owed. keepalive-electron-harness.mjs proved the fix for the case it was written for (a workspace close no longer kills a healthy server) and explicitly left this open: MediaWorkspaceHost.tsx:64's remount logic was BELIEVED to cover a mid-session death but nothing had killed a sidecar and watched the renderer re-provision.
twoRoutesDriven: crash — taskkill /F on the child from outside the app, so the supervisor learns of it through child.on('exit') and reports `offline` carrying the exit code, not `stopped`
dev-panel restart — seanimeStop() then seanimeStart(); the panel has no single restart button
phase6CrashRestartPath.thePhaseThatHadNeverBeenAsked: startSeanime() calls keepalive.start() on every ready, but only the FIRST generation of a session had ever been observed holding a client. If it armed once per session the fix would protect one sidecar and quietly hand every later one back to the dead-man switch — and a crash is exactly when a user next closes the workspace. All four generations log `Client connected id=study-os-supervisor`, and the RESTARTED sidecar survives 35s alone where the module harness measured an unprotected one exiting after 14,268 ms.
phase6CrashRestartPath.aTokenInLocalStorageIsNotProof: atomWithStorage(..., {getOnInit: true}) snapshotted localStorage at module-eval, which on a restart happened long ago, so 'the stored token changed' only proves seanimeBootstrap ran — not that the adopted client uses it. The decisive check is server-side: /events validates ?token=, so a websocket the NEW server accepted could only have carried the new hash. Use that shape for any future re-provisioning claim.
phase6CrashRestartPath.newFindingRecordedNotFixed: While the media workspace is OPEN, the dev panel's Stop button cannot stop the sidecar — MediaWorkspaceHost's [open, status] recovery effect restarts it within seconds (949 ms and 5,720 ms across runs, with no start call from the harness). Defensible, since an open workspace is when the app wants a media server, but undocumented — and it made the first cut of phase E measure something other than what it claimed. Phase E now runs with the workspace CLOSED; phase E0 records the open case deliberately.
probeCorrections: Sampled the server log ONCE, right after `ready`. keepalive.start() runs just BEFORE setStatus({kind:'ready'}), so at that instant the socket is still in flight; a single read reported `keepalive false` for a generation whose connect line landed a second later. Now polled by waitForKeepalive().

Read a log file from a process the harness had just killed. An earlier cut closed the workspace ~1s after a revival and killed that sidecar seconds later; its log ended mid-startup with no client lines, which read as 'a revived generation never gets a keepalive' — a defect that does not exist. Absence of a line in a TRUNCATED log is not absence of the event, and status.logTail cannot settle it either: pushLog keeps 40 lines and the sidecar's startup stdout pushes the keepalive line out every time.

phase6ContinueWatching.firstJoinOfTheTwoResumeStores: Study OS's legacy Media Center writes MediaItem.positionSec/lastPlayedAt; VideoCore writes its own entries under a different key. Two players, two positions for one file, and no surface had ever reconciled them. Newest write wins — preferring one player unconditionally would silently discard the session the user just finished — and a library position with no lastPlayedAt timestamps as 0, so a real VideoCore write always outranks an undated one.
honestyRules: Only `file:` resume keys become rows. videoCoreResumeKey also mints media:, stream: and playback:, and a playbackId is minted fresh on every open (the same refusal watchLoopSourceKey makes). Decisively, the only way to reopen a local file is MediaWorkspaceOpenRequest.localFilePath, so a row from any other key would render a control that cannot work. Excluded, NOT rendered disabled.

A percentage is reported only when a duration was measured. The resume store holds positionSec and nothing else; MediaItem.durationSec exists only where Study OS probed the file. Rows without one state the timestamp, which is a fact. Inventing a denominator to fill the bar is the 1x1-GIF shape in miniature.

`Finished` needs a duration to be knowable. With one, a file within 30s of its end is dropped. Without one no claim is made and the row stays — not a gap, because StudyPlayerSlice already clears its resume entry near EOF.

Card counts come from mining provenance, never from Anki. Partly cost (a widget on a 30s timer cannot afford an interval snapshot over a real collection) but decisively slice 6's rule: with Anki unreachable every Anki-derived number becomes a confident zero. Maturity and attention stay in the Review panel.
Below 10s of position, `continue` and `start` are the same action, so the row is noise — the legacy player writes a position for anything it opens, including a file glanced at and closed.

threeConnections.widgetRowToPlayer: MEDIA_WORKSPACE_OPEN_EVENT with an EXPLICIT startAtSec (position minus a 5s rewind for context). Explicit rather than relying on the stored resume, so this path does not depend on the reopen-while-active resume behaviour still recorded as measured-but-unexplained.
threeConnections.widgetPillToReview: STUDY_REVIEW_FOCUS_EVENT with the join key. That event previously only came from a readiness row inside an already-open workspace, so the host never had to open itself; from the desktop it would have set a view behind a launcher the user is still looking at. MediaWorkspaceHost now opens too — pinned by a test VERIFIED to fail on the pre-fix structure.
threeConnections.paletteToPlayer: A Continue watching group in the palette's search mode. The palette builds its list in the tick it opens and has no budget to await seanimeStatus(), so mediaWorkspaceHostIsMounted() asks the DOM for `.seanime-host-launcher, .seanime-host` instead: presence of the listener established by presence of the thing that owns it. With the flag off the group is simply absent rather than dead.

phase6WatchToReviewLoop.whatItIs: The return path of a loop whose outbound half has existed since 03d27a3. Mining writes a full VideoCoreCueProvenance for every exported card; nothing ever read it back. watch -> mine -> review in Anki -> come back to the exact line. New Review segment in MediaWorkspaceHost, so the switch is Library / Readiness / Review.

honestyRules: An interval is NOT a due date and this never pretends otherwise — same rule and reason as reviewForecast.ts. Cards are described by maturity. anki:dueForecast does know due-ness but answers collection-wide, so it cannot be attributed to one title and is deliberately unused.

Absent from the interval snapshot is `untracked`, NOT `new`. IntervalSnapshot.sourceQueries is the union of the profiles' sync queries, so an unmatched note is never scanned at all; calling it new would report a confident zero-day interval for a card nobody looked at.

The card-to-interval join is by noteId, NEVER by expression. createVideoCoreMiningDraft sets term to the whole sentence and the user may edit it, so expression matching would fail silently on exactly the cards that matter.
Only `exported` history becomes a card. `duplicate` carries no noteId and is counted separately rather than dropped; `undone` and `failed` are excluded.
Attention is only Anki's two authoritative markers (leech, suspended). A `new` card is backlog and a rewatch does not fix not having studied it.

startAtSec.why: Without it the surface is a list, not a loop.
startAtSec.contract: Optional on MediaWorkspaceOpenRequest, normalised at the boundary (NaN/negative/non-number dropped — reaching initialState.currentTime it would read as a broken file rather than a bad request), consumed in StudyPlayerSlice's `watch` case where an explicit destination outranks the stored resume position and nothing else does.
twoTraps: `??` not `||`: a requested 0 is the top of the file and must still suppress the resume rather than fall through to it.

It applies ONLY to the file it was issued for. The request object outlives the open that consumed it, so without a key check a later `watch` for a different file would inherit someone else's timestamp and silently start it minutes in. Both sides compared through videoCoreResumeKey — the resume store's own normalisation, not a second path-comparison rule.
startAtSec.leadInWhy: Seeking to the exact startMs lands a frame or two late and clips the first mora, which is the part a struggling card usually needs.
startAtSec.provenLive: CLOSED 2026-07-30 — proof/startatsec-20260730/startatsec-seeks-a-real-video.json. Bridge-driven (no mouse/keyboard), isolated G-PLAY fixture profile, real <userData>/seanime never touched, 0 stray processes after quit, resume store restored byte-exact. The discriminator was free: the store already held positionSec 3.566411 for that exact file from the G-PLAY run, so 'startAtSec honoured' and 'stored resume honoured' predicted different landings. THREE runs, TWO distinct supplied values, each landing within 15ms and each overriding a DIFFERENT stored resume: 12.5 (store 3.566) -> play 12.5/seeking 12.5/seeked 12.515; 25.0 (store 22.2) -> play 25.0/seeking 25.0/seeked 25.006; 12.5 repeat -> seeked 12.500. Captured from a capture-phase media-event listener, not by polling.

phase6WatchToReviewLoop.reverseConnection: seanimeWatchLoopByEntry rolls cards up onto the SAME pathKey the slice-1 join produces, so a preparation row also says what watching it already produced ('12 cards mined - 3 need a look'). Absent, not zero, when nothing was mined. It has its OWN effect on purpose: the first version put the rollup fetch inside the Anki-health effect and one throwing call erased the health verdict — two existing tests caught it. focusHandoff.why: Stating '3 need a look' on a readiness row with nowhere to click is worse than not stating it — a number the user can read but not follow.
focusHandoff.mechanism: The rollup is a BUTTON raising STUDY_REVIEW_FOCUS_EVENT with {pathKey, title} — the join key, never a raw path. MediaWorkspaceHost catches it, switches to the Review segment and passes the focus down. An event rather than threaded props for the same reason MEDIA_WORKSPACE_OPEN_EVENT is one: the two panels are lazy siblings under the host and neither owns the other.
focusHandoff.loadBearing: Focus is applied to the INPUT, not the output. scopedHistory filters the mining history before the model runs, so the tiles, the attention list and the duplicate count all describe the same set. Filtering only the rendered list would leave the tiles reporting the whole library beside a single title's cards — quietly wrong in exactly the way this surface exists to prevent. Pinned by its own test.
focusHandoff.deadEndAvoided: A focus matching nothing stays clearable (the chip renders outside the content branch) and the empty state says 'No cards from this title', not the library-wide 'Nothing mined yet' — which would tell a user who has mined fifty cards that they have mined none.

alreadyMinedMarker.why: The loop's last missing arrow. While WATCHING, nothing told you a line was already a card — so you re-mine it and find out from Anki's duplicate warning, after the framing, screenshot and audio clip are all captured. That is exactly what the G-PLAY run hit.
alreadyMinedMarker.how: findMinedCueEntry — pure, over mining history already in the panel's state. No Anki call and no I/O, so it cannot stutter playback. The marker sits beside the mine result, OUTSIDE the collapsible form, so it is legible before any capture work is done.
threeRules: watchLoopSourceKey REFUSES videoCoreResumeKey's `playback:` fallback. A playbackId is a directstream id minted fresh on every open, so it can never establish that a cue was mined in an EARLIER session. Accepting it would make the lookup appear to work — it matches fine within one session, which is precisely when you least need it — and silently answer 'never mined' after every restart.

Cue identity is trackNumber + index + startMs TOGETHER. Index alone is not enough: selecting a track mid-playback restarts the stream and re-indexes from the current position (a real G-PLAY finding), so an index can point at different lines across two sessions. startMs comes from the demuxer and is stable.

`exported` and `duplicate` count as already-mined; `undone` and `failed` do NOT. A duplicate means Anki refused because the note exists. An undone card was deliberately removed, so the line is genuinely minable again — warning there would be wrong in the direction that costs the user a card.

phase6ShellHandoff.verdict: PASS — two independent instances of one defect, both measured before either fix line was written
phase6ShellHandoff.theDefect: `video.resumeLast` is a BUILT-IN (slice 11), so it is offered in every shell that mounts CommandPalette — the reader, every pop-out, the desktop. Only some of those mount MediaWorkspaceHost. The app's only test for 'can I hand a file to the player?' was mediaWorkspaceHostIsMounted(), a DOM query for `.seanime-host-launcher`, which answers 'is a host mounted AND has a non-disabled status arrived?'. Measured with the sidecar at `ready` and no host: the toast read 'The media server is off, so there is nothing to resume into.' A missing host is a fact about the WINDOW; a disabled sidecar is a fact about the MACHINE. False by default since the slice-12 flip.
phase6ShellHandoff.secondInstance: A `player` pop-out routes to the workspace (retirement step 2) but App mounted the host only for `popout === 'video'`, so the section's own open button dispatched into a window with no listener. THREE places encode 'which sections open the workspace' — AppSection's switch, the host's os:open listener, App's pop-out mount — and only the third was stale. Now one list: MEDIA_WORKSPACE_SECTIONS / sectionOpensMediaWorkspace(). A pop-out is a separate renderer with its own App tree, so 'the host is mounted' is per-window and cannot be inherited from the desktop that spawned it.
phase6ShellHandoff.presenceIsTheListenersLifetime: MediaWorkspaceHost calls registerMediaWorkspaceHost() from INSIDE the effect that adds its window listeners and releases it in that effect's cleanup. It therefore reports true a full commit BEFORE `status` arrives and the launcher renders — which is exactly the state the reader handoff creates, and exactly where the DOM marker reads false. The release is idempotent because StrictMode runs an effect's cleanup twice and a second decrement would under-count a host that is still mounted.
phase6ShellHandoff.theDomMarkerIsKept: mediaWorkspaceHostIsMounted() still gates the palette's search-mode Continue-watching group and Statistics' By-show rows. Those decide whether to OFFER a list, in the tick they render, with no room for an await — and with the sidecar disabled those rows would open a player the user never sees. Right question there, wrong one for dispatch.
phase6ShellHandoff.threeTrueStatements: no host in this window -> mediaWorkspace.resumeLast.noWorkspaceHere (new); sidecar disabled -> mediaWorkspace.resumeLast.unavailable (now only when true, answered by MAIN on the failure path only via a new non-hook mediaWorkspaceIsAvailable() that useMediaWorkspaceAvailability is written in terms of); empty store -> mediaWorkspace.resumeLast.nothing. The shell answer NEVER asks main — that is knowable without the sidecar, and asking anyway would let an IPC failure re-word a shell fact as a sidecar fact. Pinned by asserting statusCalls === 0.
phase6ShellHandoff.readerHandoff: renderer/readerResumeHandoff.ts. While a book is open App registers a handler that checks availability, closes the book, and lets the EFFECT BODY run the ordinary built-in against the desktop that just came back. Availability is checked BEFORE the close so a disabled sidecar never costs the user their book. The resume runs from the effect body rather than the handler so it lands after the commit — MediaWorkspaceHost is a child of the component running the hook and a child's effects run before its parent's, so the listener exists by then, with no sleep and no polling. It lives outside App.tsx so it can be driven against a REAL host rather than a re-creation of the shell.

blockers.status: CLOSED 2026-07-30 by explicit user decision — the user was asked (the alternative was leaving it to Phase 9) and chose to edit forge.config.ts, overriding CLAUDE.md's rule against altering root project configuration for that one file. SeanimeSidecarStagingPlugin copies the resolved binary (SEANIME_EXE, else the pinned sibling checkout) into build/seanime in prePackage, and extraResource ships that directory, which electron-packager places at <resources>/seanime by basename. A missing binary FAILS the build; SEANIME_SKIP_SIDECAR_PACKAGING=1 opts out loudly; a non-win32 target gets an empty slot instead of a .exe.

blockers.notProven: CLOSED 2026-07-31 — proof/packaged-sidecar-launch-20260731102252. The premise that this needed mouse control was wrong: --remote-debugging-port works in a packaged build and window.api.seanimeStart() is the same call MediaWorkspaceHost makes, so the run is CDP plus one IPC call with no synthetic input. It also needed no rebuild (the 2026-07-30 package is still on disk with an sha256-identical binary, so a running dev server's EBUSY is irrelevant) and no closing of the developer's app (a scratch --user-data-dir side-steps requestSingleInstanceLock). Sidecar reached ready in 1,600 ms, seanime v3.10.2, running from out/.../resources/seanime/seanime.exe, keepalive holding one established socket owned by the app's MAIN process, zero orphans on quit.
blockers.howItAvoidsAFalsePass: resolveSeanimeExe falls back to the pinned sibling checkout, which EXISTS on this machine and is byte-identical (the record carries both sha256 values and they match), so 'it reached ready' would be satisfied just as well by a silent fallback — and that fallback is exactly what would ship a dead media surface to every other machine. Two guards exclude it: SEANIME_EXE is DELETED from the child's environment rather than merely left unset (a developer shell may export it, and it wins outright), and the running seanime.exe's own ExecutablePath is read back from Windows and required to be the packaged one.
twoProbeFailuresRecorded: A packaged Electron build does not load from file:// — this one registers a custom protocol and serves app://bundle/index.html. A file://-based CDP target filter matched nothing and the run sat at the attach for its full timeout with a healthy app on screen. The filter is now scheme-agnostic, matching the shape that identifies the main desktop window (a page target with no query string), which is debugBridge.ts's own rule.

Reading the sidecar's log for `Client connected id=study-os-supervisor` reported false while the keepalive was demonstrably connected — the THIRD instance of this failure in one session. The run kills the sidecar ~30s in and a force-killed process leaves a log ending mid-startup. Phase D now measures an established TCP socket and its owning process, which cannot be truncated; the log check is corroboration only and explicitly allowed to be absent. Do not reintroduce a log-tail read as primary evidence for a short-lived process.

translationDefectsFoundAndFixed.firstDiagnosisWasWrong: It was read as 'translateRun echoes the source'. The probe passed from/to where the API takes source/target, so undefined === undefined hit a same-language short-circuit. Loaded directly from Node with the shipped buildSentencePrompt, Qwen_Qwen3-1.7B-Q4_K_M.gguf translates 猫が窓辺で寝ている。 to 'A cat is sleeping on the window ledge.' in ~800ms. fixed: translateText compared the language pair without validating it, so a missing or unknown code returned the source text as a successful translation. It now rejects an unrecognized or non-string code (src/main/__tests__/translateGuards.test.ts).

translateSentence never applied isValidCrossLangTranslation, which the batch path always had. It now validates, retries once with the strict prompt, and yields nothing rather than an echo; translateText drops an untranslatable sentence instead of back-filling source text, and throws when none survive.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE OF THE BOGUS CACHES: translateMokuroPage returned the page unchanged when no region translated and analyzeMangaVolume cached it anyway, so refreshMangaOcrMeta counted it as translated. Nothing surfaced because runTranslationBatch reports a failed item as an empty string. Now the page is cached only when a region really translated, an echoed source is rejected at the persistence boundary too, and analyzeMangaVolume returns a warning the reader shows (src/main/__tests__/mangaOcrTranslateCache.test.ts).

keyDecisions.joinByPath: Absolute path, normalised via studyLibraryPathKey (case-fold, separators, trailing separator), ONE DIRECTION, nothing written back to either store. It is the only fact both libraries record independently — Anime_LocalFile.path (types.ts:1710) and MediaItem.path (shared/types.ts:112). Matches the risk register mitigation "external-id columns only, one direction".
keyDecisions.pathFormatIsNotGuaranteed: The one real Seanime path on record (proof/gplay-20260728/) is native Windows with backslashes, same as Study OS — but that is ONE sample from ONE fixture library and the sidecar is a Go process. Hence normalisation rather than trusting the observation.
keyDecisions.unlinkedIsItsOwnState: In the Seanime library but never imported into Study OS. Deliberately distinct from unanalyzed (imported, not analysed) and missing-subtitles. Collapsing them sends the user to the wrong action; a test pins it.
keyDecisions.readyIsStrict: ready requires analyzer version, subtitleReady, all three fingerprints, AND the snapshot subtitleRecordId matching the attached Japanese track. Anything less is stale, which still carries the snapshot but must never be shown as current. An ABSENT frequencyListsFingerprint counts as a mismatch, not a match.
keyDecisions.queueOrder: seanimeStudyPreparationQueue excludes ready and orders by least work: unanalyzed -> stale -> missing-subtitles -> unlinked; ties keep incoming order.

Tests pin both.

Success is verified by checking the item actually arrived under its join key; the skip gets its own message ("Study OS does not recognise that file type") instead of a success that did nothing. Three things must hold, each failure reported separately because each has a different fix: disconnected (Anki unreachable; the reason is carried through when Anki gave one), no-decks (connected but nothing to mine into), no-profile (nothing routes a subtitle card). disconnected is reported ahead of no-decks: an unreachable Anki has no decks to report, so the deck count is not evidence of anything.

retirementStep3_20260731.defectFound: Phase B found that MediaWorkspaceHost and MediaWorkspaceSectionView were BOTH opening the workspace. The host has listened for os:open 'video' since Phase 2; the section's first cut also dispatched on mount, so video opened twice and — because that dispatch waits on an async seanimeStatus() round trip — a close inside that window was undone by the late dispatch. It also meant a restored desktop layout threw a full-screen overlay up at boot with no user action. FIXED: the host's listener is the single owner and now covers 'player' too; the mount dispatch is gone; the panel's button still dispatches because that is an explicit request.
probeCorrections: A cold profile shows the consent screen and `.consent` covers the viewport, so phase B first reported 'no draggable point on the title bar' — which reads exactly like the drag-layer defect it exists to catch. querySelector and .click() do not hit-test, which is why earlier harnesses never noticed. Consent is declined before any pointer-driven phase.
A prepared datadir is SINGLE-USE for playback: re-running against one that has already served a session hangs on 'Opening local file'. Build a fresh one per run.

terminateRaceAnswered.guard1: stream.go:467 — while the replacement is PREPARING (currentStream empty), a terminate whose key.PlaybackID == m.replacedPlaybackId is ignored ('replaced playback session during preparation'). replacedPlaybackId is set in BeginOpenWithTarget only when a previous stream existed.

thenWiredAndRevertedAgain.mistake2_theImportantOne: The stage fired CORRECTLY and was destructive anyway — the fire condition was never the problem. thenTheIntermittencyWasDIAGNOSED_AND_FIX.itWasNotBlanc: it looked like a property of Blanc ("subtitle delivery drops cue 1 in ~40% of runs") and was a property of the code MEASURING Blanc.
thenTheIntermittencyWasDIAGNOSED_AND_FIX.theBug: phase I re-seeked +/-0.05 s up to 20 times "to re-trigger delivery" when no cue was active. That loop was SELF-DEFEATING. Sidecar source: SeekedEvent -> startSubtitleStreamForTime (stream.go:553) -> beginSubtitleSeek (subtitles.go:316, STOPS every active subtitle stream) -> restart at subtitleOffsetForTime (subtitles.go:206), which applies a 10-SECOND PREROLL before snapping to an MKV cue position: max(currentTime - 10, 0). At the 7.3 s park that is 0 — the start of the file — and +/-0.05 s cannot move it. So every nudge stopped the in-flight parser and restarted it from byte 0, where it re-delivers cue 0. Twenty nudges, twenty restarts, cue 1 never reached.
thenTheIntermittencyWasDIAGNOSED_AND_FIX.differentialEvidence: retirement-step3 phase E parks at the same 7.3 s, seeks ONCE, waits 1500 ms, never re-seeks -> 7/7 PASS. blanc-player phase I with the nudge loop -> 4 PASS / 3 FAIL. blanc-player phase I with the loop removed -> 3/3 PASS (proof/blanc-player-live-20260801114*, cue 1 active every time at index 1 / startMs 6500, R -> 6.5197, W -> 2.00x, S -> 6.5x).
thenTheIntermittencyWasDIAGNOSED_AND_FIX.fix: deleted the re-seek, kept the poll.
thenTheIntermittencyWasDIAGNOSED_AND_FIX.generalLesson: A RETRY THAT RE-ISSUES THE TRIGGERING ACTION IS NOT A RETRY, IT IS A RESET. Here the action being retried (seek) is the very thing that discards the progress being waited for. Every other harness in docs/migration/tools that "nudges to re-trigger" is worth re-reading against that.
thenTheIntermittencyWasDIAGNOSED_AND_FIX.doesNotOverturn: the stage-2 attribution. Phase E, the main-window equivalent, seeks once and passes 7 of 7 unwired versus 1 of 3 with the re-opening stage — so that difference is not this race.

defect.why: A write of 0 is not neutral: resolveVideoCoreResumePosition returns 0 for any stored entry below 1s, and seanimeContinueWatching drops any row under CONTINUE_WATCHING_MIN_POSITION_SEC (10s). A zero deletes the resume point and the Continue Watching row together.
defect.ambiguity: video.currentTime === 0 means BOTH "the user is at the top of the file" and "there is no media here at all". video-core.tsx 965-970 empties the element (pause / removeAttribute("src") / load()) whenever playbackInfo goes null, which our own open-and-await branch does on EVERY open.
reachableSequences: open an episode with a stored 8.8, leave before a frame decodes (or hit the silent-open stall): pre-slice stored 0, shipped stores 8.8
play to 528, element emptied by the lifecycle effect, teardown lands after it: pre-slice stored 0, shipped stores 528

rule.skip: the element has no media, or the position is sub-threshold and this session never started — the write knows nothing the store does not
rule.clear: ended, inside the end margin, or a sub-threshold position from a session that HAD started (a rewind to 0:00 after eight minutes is a decision; an unplayed 0 is not)
rule.hasMedia: read off the element as readyState > 0 || currentSrc !== '' — the exact signal the lifecycle effect destroys, and sound because VideoCore attaches the stream as a src attribute (video-core.tsx:443)

resumeControlRun20260801.designCorrectionWorthMoreThanThePhase: A REWIND CANNOT CONSTRUCT A NEVER-STARTED SESSION — sessionMaxSec spans the whole ResumeTracker effect, so a rewind after real playback is the DELIBERATE case slice 35 clears on purpose. Nor can clearing the store by hand: run 1 proved the teardown rewrites it between dispatch and watch. The setup therefore USES that mechanism — rewind below the floor so the teardown CLEARS, then the next open starts at 0 and its session max stays under the floor. A pause guard is required because openFileWithRetry waits for readyState >= 2 while an autoplaying element runs on; it cannot suppress the restore, since restoreSeekTime only calls play/pause for an explicit boolean and canplay fires either way. openGenerationPatch20260801.what: patches/seanime/0004-directstream-open-generation.patch — a client-supplied generation the SIDECAR can refuse, consulted BEFORE BeginOpen. The half of the stale-open problem a client cannot do.
openGenerationPatch20260801.closes: The sentence slices 32, 37 and 39 all end at: a recovery request already sent CANNOT BE RECALLED — fetch abort abandons the response, never the work — so it can land inside a later open and BeginOpen -> beginSubtitleSeek strips that open subtitles. Slice 32 named the only two fixes: a generation the sidecar can reject, or a client rule that never issues while a newer open is outstanding. shared/directstreamOpenChannel.ts is the second; this is the FIRST.

rule.api: Manager.AcceptOpenGeneration(clientId, generation), called before BeginOpen — after it the damage is already done
rule.unspecified: 0, negative, or no client id -> ACCEPTED and records nothing, so every existing client is unaffected
rule.equal: ACCEPTED — a re-open of the SAME request is the legitimate recovery this protects, not a stale one
rule.older: REFUSED, with an error, before BeginOpen runs
rule.other: clients are ordered independently; a refusal does not move the bar

openGenerationPatch20260801.inertOnPurpose: Nothing sends generation — not Study OS, not upstream — so applying the patch changes NO observable behaviour. That is what makes the server half landable and verifiable alone, while the client half (generation: requestId on the open body and on every recovery for that request) stays a separate, live-measured step. For the same reason it is NOT in build-patched-sidecar.mjs patch list; adding it there is the wiring session call.

machineTraps: Git Bash tar cannot extract to a Windows path — git archive | tar -C C:\... fails with "Cannot connect to C: resolve failed" because it reads C: as a remote host. Both tools use git clone instead, which also gives the diff a .git to be taken against. build-patched-sidecar.mjs was believed to get away with tar.exe because that resolves to System32 — CORRECTED IN SLICE 46: that was a fact about the shell it had been run from, not about the tool, and from Git Bash it dies the same way. It now spawns System32 tar.exe by its absolute %SystemRoot% path.

git clone honours the global core.autocrlf, so the tree comes out CRLF, every multi-line anchor stops matching, and a patch generated from it would carry line-ending churn into an upstream-submittable diff. Both tools clone and check out with -c core.autocrlf=false. Slice 39 CRLF lesson arriving from a completely different direction on the same day.

openGenerationWireGate20260802.whyTwoBinaries: A refusal has NO positive observable. PlayLocalFile returns before BeginOpen, so the defer that would call AbortOpen is never registered and nothing is logged; and both outcomes answer a byte-identical 500 {"message":"Internal Server Error"} because echo's default error handler runs with e.Debug = false and Seanime installs no request-logging middleware. Reading the missing marker as the finding would be the absence-of-a-line trap this track has paid for three times. The verdict is the DIFFERENCE between two binaries on identical input; each absence is bracketed by its own HTTP response and by the control's presence. A step with neither marker nor response fails as INCONCLUSIVE.
openGenerationWireGate20260802.latentHazard: A client cannot tell a correct refusal from a real failure — both are that opaque 500. Harmless today BY CONSTRUCTION, not by design: the launch path always posts the newest generation, so the only refusable launch POST is one whose fetch the supersession already aborted (StudyPlayerSlice.tsx:802 returns without reporting), and a recovery re-sends the launch's own generation, which is the equal case. One changed assumption and a legitimate refusal reaches the user-visible error at StudyPlayerSlice.tsx:798. If 0004 goes upstream, a distinguishable status or error body belongs in it.

slice47e.title: the profile allow-list is enforced where the effect happens, not only where the plan is made
slice47e.defect: evaluateAgentToolAccess took only the permission LEVEL. The per-profile enabledOperations allow-list was checked ONLY in parseLocalAgentModelPlan - plan time - while executeAgentTaskStep re-checked the level alone. AgentTasks are persisted in AgentTaskQueue (up to 100 items, with paused/resumed states), so a task planned while a profile enabled flashcard.delete-deck stayed runnable after the user removed that operation from the profile.
slice47e.fix: evaluateAgentToolAccess takes an optional allowedOperations and both boundaries call the one rule, so they cannot drift apart. AgentExecutionOptions carries it; both renderer call sites pass activeProfile?.enabledOperations. Optional rather than required so a caller with genuinely no profile is still governed by the permission level alone rather than denied everything by an allow-list it never set.
slice47e.verification: The new test was confirmed NON-VACUOUS: with the guard temporarily removed it fails with "expected completed to be failed", i.e. the handler ran. Three tests: the narrowed profile refuses, an enabled operation still runs, and a caller with no profile is unaffected.
slice47e.audit: agent-allowlist-enforced-only-at-plan-time - checks the guard at the EXECUTION site specifically, because a fix that only re-tightened the parser would leave the persisted-task path exactly as it was.

slice58.title: the refusal finally came, and slice56's fix had a second bug only the live gate could see
slice58.verdict: PASS, exit 0, step 10 in its STRONG form - proof/phase7-queue-refusal-20260802slice58b/
slice58.measured: narrowed arm: dictionary.search-knowledge -> failed, error 'Search local knowledge is not enabled for the active agent profile.'; control arm: the same step from the same persisted plan -> completed, error null. Same plan, same restart, one variable. This is the first time 47e's allow-list, 51's queue wiring and 56's profile merge have been shown working TOGETHER against shipped bytes.
slice58.theSecondBug: normalizeAgentProfiles emitted disabledOperations: [] on EVERY profile it returned. Once a store had been through it those empty arrays persisted, and the legacy guard tested !== undefined - so it read [] as 'already a delta', skipped the conversion of a plain enabledOperations edit, and let the factory's 19 operations win. The gate narrows by mutating enabledOperations on exactly such a stored object.
slice58.whyTheUnitTestsMissedIt: Every slice56 test hands normalizeAgentProfiles a HAND-WRITTEN store. The app hands it one that has ALREADY BEEN NORMALIZED ONCE. That gap is now its own test: 'survives the real sequence: load, save, narrow, load again'.
slice58.fix: Both directions, because either alone leaves a sharp edge: empty deltas are no longer EMITTED at all (an unedited profile round-trips indistinguishable from one never edited), and an empty delta is no longer TREATED as a delta on input.
slice58.transferableLesson: A normalizer's OUTPUT SHAPE is an input to its next run. Any function that both reads and writes the same persisted structure must be tested on its own output, not only on hand-written fixtures. A round-trip test is not optional for this shape.
slice58.theDetour: The first run after the rebuild still FAILED, and the gate's own step-10 text named normalizeAgentProfiles discarding built-in edits - the defect slice56 had already fixed. Three things had to be separated: (a) that text was HARDCODED by slice53 and re-derives nothing, asserting a fixed cause with full confidence - it has now been rewritten to report the observation and stop, and to say why naming a cause there is a mistake; (b) the fix HAD shipped, verified in resources/app/.vite/.../BlancShell-*.js with a known-shipped control (slice52's music.controls.volume) so a search matching nothing could not read as absence; (c) targetEnabled=false is computed by READ_STORAGE from RAW localStorage, so it only ever meant 'the narrowing is on disk', never 'the app honoured it'. A further theory - that activeProfile resolved to undefined and bypassed the allow-list - was also wrong, since getActiveAgentProfile always returns a profile. Reading the gate's SOURCE instead of reasoning further is what found the real cause.

slice56.title: every edit to a built-in agent profile was being discarded on load
slice56.defect: normalizeAgentProfiles seeded its map with the four factory built-ins (localAgentProfiles.ts:146) and then continued on any stored profile whose id was already present (:151) - which is every built-in id. A stored edit to a built-in was silently discarded on EVERY load.
slice56.measuredLive: Slice53 drove it end to end: narrow a profile from 19 operations to 18, restart, run the queued task -> status completed, error null, IDENTICAL to the control. Its probe agent-profile-narrowing-probe.mjs confirmed the mechanism with a control on a CUSTOM profile, where the same edit does persist.
slice56.whyItMattered: Slice47e's execution-time allow-list re-check is correct and was UNREACHABLE on a built-in profile, and the four built-ins are all a fresh user has. A user narrowing a built-in's permissions got no feedback and no protection.
slice56.productDecision: The fork was what happens when a future version adds an operation to a built-in the user has edited. Storing the user's list wholesale freezes that profile forever; discarding it is what caused the bug. The user delegated the call; operations are now stored as a DELTA.
slice56.rule: identity (id, name, description, role, builtIn) stays FACTORY-owned so a future version can re-word a built-in and a stored entry cannot impersonate one; preferences (permission, model, response/explanation/language/teaching/correction, enabled) are the USER's and override outright; operations are disabledOperations/addedOperations applied over the CURRENT factory list, never a frozen copy - so a narrowing always sticks AND a newly added factory operation still appears.
slice56.legacyConversion: A store written before the delta carries a whole enabledOperations list that has never once taken effect. On load it is converted to the equivalent delta, so an earlier edit finally applies. Both directions honoured, but only for operations still in ALL_OPERATIONS, so an operation the product has since removed cannot be resurrected by a stale list.
slice56.nonVacuity: src/shared/__tests__/localAgentProfileOverrides.test.ts - 11 tests written first, 6 FAILING before the change and 5 passing. The 5 are the control block and they are the point: an untouched store still yields the exact factory operations, custom profiles are untouched, all four built-ins survive an override, and an unknown id in a delta changes nothing. Without them a normalizer returning the factory list for everything would be green forever. getActiveAgentProfile is asserted DIRECTLY, because it is what hands allowedOperations to the single renderer execution boundary.
slice56.stillOpen: The settings UI still writes a whole enabledOperations list, which the legacy path converts on load. That works, but the round-trip only stabilises onto the delta after one save. Having the UI write the delta directly is a clean follow-up.

slice51.title: the persisted agent queue was a dead end, and now it runs
slice51.handoff: docs/migration/SLICE_51_PHASE7_QUEUE.md - the full write-up lives there because another agent held NEXT_SESSION.md during the concurrent Phase 9 run
slice51.verdict: slice48's structural finding CONFIRMED and FIXED
slice51.evidence: nextRunnableAgentQueueItem had exactly two references repo-wide - its definition at src/shared/localAgentTaskQueue.ts:90 and its own test. No production module referenced it, and no setTask call took a queue item: every pre-fix writer in BlancReadyToolPanels.tsx was 276 (declaration), 308 (setTask(null)), 326 (plan response), 586 and 618 (execution results). Both verbs opened with if (!task) return. The queue rows offered exactly four controls - Pause, Resume, Cancel, Prioritize. There was no fifth.
slice51.correctionToSlice48: slice48 recorded this as a CROSS-SESSION problem. It stranded work WITHIN a session too: plan() clears task at 308 and overwrites it at 326 while appending every plan to the queue at 327, so planning a second objective stranded the first permanently. Dead rows accumulated from the second plan onward, not the second session onward.
slice51.howThisReReads47e: 47e's motivating story - a task planned while a profile enabled flashcard.delete-deck staying runnable after the operation is removed - was describing a path that COULD NOT EXECUTE. Slice51 makes it real for the first time, which is exactly why the fix had to carry the allow-list rather than bolt a setTask onto a queue row.
slice51.fix: new src/renderer/localAgentQueueRun.ts: selectAgentQueueRun, pendingAgentTaskStep, runAgentTaskStep, applyAgentRunToQueue, agentQueueStatusForTask. The panel routes all three verbs through one runStep helper and gained a per-row Run plus a Run next queued plan button whose disabled state is computed by the same selector the click uses, so enablement and action cannot disagree.
slice51.allowListInvariant: STRENGTHENED, not widened. The renderer's execution boundaries went from TWO to ONE - executeAgentTaskStep was called at BlancReadyToolPanels.tsx:578 and :609 and is now called once inside runAgentTaskStep. allowedOperations is a REQUIRED property of AgentQueueRunOptions typed to admit undefined, so a caller must state what the profile permits and cannot silently omit it into full access; it stays optional on AgentExecutionOptions, as 47e intended, with a test pinning that. A structural test fails any future verb that calls the executor directly.
slice51.nonVacuity: The structural half failed 3/3 pre-fix with a 3-test control block that passed (proving the walker resolves real modules, that the test-file exclusion does work, and that an invented symbol reports absent). The behavioural half's only pre-fix failure was 'Cannot find module', which proves the FIXTURE and not the code - so it was checked by MUTATION instead: reverting just the allow-list pass-through gives 'expected vi.fn() to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times'. The deck-deletion handler ran, the same signature 47e reported.

slice51.gates: 361 files / 4589 tests pass; i18n 6436 keys exit 0; architecture 1331 modules, 18 findings, nothing new. Verified independently against the tree, including that exactly three src files were touched and the slice-48/49 storage files were never opened.

slice48.whereTheModelBites: Located by a differential, because a refusal has no positive observable: agent disabled -> 'The local agent is disabled in Settings.' (0ms); enabled but modelFileName pointed at a file that does not exist -> 'No local GGUF model was found.' (1ms). Two DIFFERENT refusals from the same call. Model-gated: producing a plan at all, and therefore step-level preview, run, confirm and every AgentExecutionEvent, because they all hang off the in-memory task that only plan() sets. NOT model-gated: the whole persisted-queue surface, the profile and permission selects, and the refusal itself.
slice48.permissionOrdering: Under limited-actions a confirming operation is DENIED, never held. Every confirming operation in AGENT_TOOL_OPERATIONS requires full-automation, and evaluateAgentToolAccess checks the permission level BEFORE the confirmation reason (localAgent.ts:231,237). The confirm path was reached by switching profile, not by faking a plan.
slice48.structuralFinding: The persisted AgentTaskQueue is a DEAD END. With two tasks in the queue, Run next approved step and Confirm sensitive step both read disabled=true - they are gated on the component's in-memory task, and the only writers of task are plan() and a previous executeAgentTaskStep (BlancReadyToolPanels.tsx:308,326,586,618). Nothing sets task from a queue item, and nextRunnableAgentQueueItem (localAgentTaskQueue.ts:90) is referenced only by its own test. The queue's paused/resumed states, 100-item cap and persistence describe work that can be listed and cancelled but never resumed into execution. This is a positive read of `disabled`, not an argument from a missing button - both controls are always rendered.
slice48.howThisRereadsSlice47e: 47e's allow-list re-check at the execution boundary is still correct and still needed WITHIN a session - plan, narrow the profile, run - but the cross-session case its comment describes ('a queued task outlives the profile that authorized it') cannot arise today, because a task that outlives the session cannot be run at all.
slice48.doesNotShow: The packaged build is 2026-08-01 and PREDATES slice 47e - allowedOperations is absent from its bundle - so the allow-list re-check itself was not exercised. Re-run after the next npm run package. Only two objectives were put to the model; which operations a 1.7B model proposes is not something this gate controls. The one step that executed a handler FAILED on a real precondition, so this run says the surfaces work, not that the agent did useful work.

slice53.title: 47e's original story driven live for the first time, and a new plan-contract defect found on the way
slice53.gate: docs/migration/tools/phase7-queue-refusal-live-gate.mjs (new). Plans LIVE through the real local model with the operation enabled, forks the persisted profile directory into two identical copies, narrows ONE of them, restarts BOTH, runs the same queued row in each, and compares. A refusal read on its own proves nothing - a step can fail for a dozen reasons that would all print a red line - so the verdict is the DIFFERENCE between two arms from identical persisted input.
slice53.languageIndependence: slice52 translated this panel and slice51 structural test had asserted the literal English word Run. Nothing in this gate matches UI prose. Navigation uses the app own toolbox:open-tool CustomEvent; the panel is found by SHAPE (the only surface with a full-automation option); the objective box is textarea[maxlength=500][rows=4] (rows matters - the scheduled-automation section carries a second maxlength=500 textarea); the action group is the .blanc-row-actions holding exactly four buttons; a queue row Run button is the first button in that row action cell. NO new data- handles were needed, so it runs against the already-packaged artifact with no rebuild.
slice53.newDefectFound: parseLocalAgentModelPlan rejects the ENTIRE plan when a step omits arguments (localAgentPrompt.ts:137) and applies that rule to operations that TAKE NO ARGUMENTS. Asked to list flashcard deck folders, Qwen3-1.7B chose flashcard.list-decks - legal, allow-listed, zero-argument, and it CLEARED evaluateAgentToolAccess at :128 - then omitted the empty arguments:{} the operation does not need. Result: "Local model step 1 needs an arguments object." and no plan at all. The system prompt does show arguments:{} in its shape example so the model is out of spec, but the failure mode is a total plan rejection citing a field the operation does not use, and the recommended local stack is exactly the size of model that omits it. One-line fix (arguments: step.arguments ?? {} or make the check conditional on the operation declaring parameters). NOT fixed here - no src edit was in scope for slice53.
slice53.profileStoreNotPersisted: A second live-only discovery: loadLocalAgentProfiles() falls back to the built-in profiles IN MEMORY and never writes them, so on a fresh install jp-study-local-agent-profiles-v1 does not exist in localStorage at all. The first gate run read activeProfileId null and would have narrowed nothing. You cannot remove an operation from a profile that was never saved. The gate now drives the panel own profile picker to another profile and back, which makes changeProfile call saveLocalAgentProfiles - so the store that lands on disk is the app own, not the gate idea of it.
slice53.verdict: The story ran end to end and THE REFUSAL NEVER CAME. proof/phase7-queue-refusal-20260802slice53e: step3 PASS (live plan, dictionary.search-knowledge args {query:neko}, attempt 1), step5 OK (planning process exited CLEANLY code 0), step7 PASS (row=queued in both arms - the queued task survived the restart), step8 PASS (19->18 and targetEnabled=false AFTER the restart), step9 PASS (clicked:Run in both arms - the per-row control slice51 built), step10 FAIL - narrowed arm step COMPLETED with error null, identically to the control.
slice53.rootCause: normalizeAgentProfiles() DISCARDS every user edit to a BUILT-IN profile. localAgentProfiles.ts:146 seeds its map with EMPTY_AGENT_PROFILE_STORE.profiles, then :151 does if (!id || byId.has(id)) continue - which skips the persisted copy of all four built-ins. loadLocalAgentProfiles() normalizes on every read and getActiveAgentProfile() normalizes AGAIN, so the panel activeProfile is the factory profile no matter what the user saved. The allow-list is NOT the bug: evaluateAgentToolAccess is wired exactly as 47e left it and runAgentTaskStep is the single renderer boundary slice51 made it - the narrowing never REACHES it.
slice53.rootCauseMeasured: docs/migration/tools/agent-profile-narrowing-probe.mjs (new, exit 0, verdict CONFIRMED). Transpiles the REAL src module with the repo own esbuild rather than reading the code and asserting. 18 ops persisted -> 19 ops after normalizeAgentProfiles() -> 19 ops from getActiveAgentProfile(). CONTROL: the identical edit on a CUSTOM profile survives at 18 ops, which is what makes the BUILT-IN ID the attributable cause rather than editing profiles being broken generally.
slice53.howThisReReads47eAThirdTime: slice48 found the queue could not be run. slice51 wired it, which made 47e story REACHABLE. slice53 drove it and found the story still cannot happen, for a different reason one layer further out: 47e execution-time re-check is correct and UNREACHABLE on a built-in profile, and the four built-ins are the only profiles a fresh user has. A user who narrows a built-in profile gets no refusal ever; only a profile created through Create profile (createLocalAgentProfile, which mints a custom- id) can be narrowed at all.
slice53.notFixed: The fix is in src/shared/localAgentProfiles.ts and is a real design decision, not a typo - built-in profiles are presumably re-seeded so a new app version can add operations to them. Merging persisted edits over the defaults per-profile is the obvious shape but needs a rule for what happens when a built-in gains an operation the user never saw. A slice of its own. NO src file was edited in slice53.

slice47g.title: the packaged CSP is readable by a test

slice52.title: every range slider carries an accessible name, and the agent panel is translated
slice52.recordedBy: NOT by slice52 itself - the run hit its account's usage limit at 14:58 having done all the work and none of the recording. Written afterwards from the tree, with the gates run by hand. SECOND run in one session to die after changing the repo: check the tree, not the log.
slice52.sliderFix: A shared primitive src/renderer/components/ui/Slider.tsx whose props make the accessible name REQUIRED AT THE TYPE LEVEL - a union of {'aria-label': string} and {'aria-labelledby': string}, not an optional ?: - so a nameless <Slider> cannot compile. Stronger than labelling each call site. 20 component files converted.
slice52.gate: src/renderer/__tests__/sliderAccessibleName.test.ts - approximates the accname algorithm in precedence order (aria-labelledby > aria-label > label[for] > wrapping label) and DELIBERATELY REJECTS title, which is only the last-resort fallback and is not announced by every screen reader.
slice52.nonVacuity: The gate carries an explicit floor - controls.length >= 55 and at least 8 <Slider> call sites - so an empty pass cannot be silent. Slice52 measured 48 raw range inputs plus 8 Slider sites. A fourth describe block tests THAT THE ANALYSER DETECTS WHAT IT CLAIMS TO, so a scanner silently matching nothing could not stay green. The primitive's own definition is exempt (nameless by construction, the name arrives from the caller) and that exemption is paid for by pinning the TYPE instead, because tsc is not a gate here.
slice52.i18n: The agent panel was half-converted - slice51's six new strings were raw English and so were their siblings Pause/Resume/Cancel/Prioritize. It now goes through t() throughout. Catalogs grew 6436 -> 6587 keys, all four languages filled.
slice52.i18nCheckCannotSeeThis: tools/i18n-check.cjs only compares keys that ALREADY EXIST, so raw literals pass it silently. Exit 0 is necessary, not sufficient - the sweep has to be done by reading the component.
slice52.breakageWorthKeeping: Converting the panel broke slice51's own structural test, which asserted the literal English word 'Run' appeared after <legend>Task queue</legend>. Two lessons: an assertion coupled to English text fails the moment the app is translated AND says nothing about whether the control does anything; and it was VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION, because indexOf returns -1 when the legend changes and slice(-1) then tests a single character instead of failing loudly. It now asserts the wiring - a queue row passes item.id to runQueued, and runQueued goes through selectAgentQueueRun.
slice52.gates: 362 files / 4599 tests pass; i18n 6587 keys exit 0; architecture 18 findings 'Nothing new' exit 0; audit-carried-items exit 0. All measured by hand after the run died.
slice52.notProvenInAnArtifact: The current out/ build predates this change, so the slider fix is proven IN SOURCE ONLY. packaged-a11y-deep-gate.mjs should be re-run after the next npm run package to confirm the volume slider announces a name in a shipped build - the same 'proven in source is not proven in the artifact' gap slices 46 and 49 both paid for.

DONE by slices 60-61 for the FOCUS RING, and the finding is that B3 had been a FALSE GREEN. The gate's colour parser read rgb()/rgba() only; Chrome computes color-mix() - which this app uses everywhere - to color(srgb r g b / a), so any boundary declared that way scored as ABSENT rather than weak. B3 was reporting PASS off the 2 stops that happened to use plain rgb(); the real population is 52 and 23 were failing. All 23 were one token: theme/tokens.css:195 --focus-ring-color at 70% accent, compositing to rgb(186,39,64) on the taskbar's --panel = 2.89:1, and every failure sat in .os-taskbar. THREE INSTRUMENT FIXES came with it, each of which had been manufacturing a wrong answer: (a) color(srgb ...) is now parsed (components 0-1, unlike rgb) - the systemic one, affecting every colour read; (b) box-shadow is now a boundary candidate alongside border and fill, strongest carrying the verdict with losers kept as ringRatio/borderRatio/fillRatio; (c) EVERY shadow layer is scanned rather than the first, and an OFFSET counts as a boundary - this app puts a soft drop shadow first and the indicator second, and .os-set-nav-item.active marks selection with a 2px inset LEFT BAR that a spread-only test can never see. Rows also record rawBoxShadow/rawBorderWidths/rawBorderStyles so a null ratio can be told apart from a boundary the probe failed to parse; that distinction ended a three-attempt guessing loop and must not be removed.

slice47h.title: the packaged CSP is delivered AND enforced
slice47h.measured: app://bundle/index.html serves a 527-char header byte-identical to shared/contentSecurityPolicy.ts; script-src is [self] with no unsafe-eval; an inline <script> is REFUSED with violatedDirective script-src-elem and does not run.
slice47h.whyItMatters: PHASE_6_5_AUDIT.md section 3 chained High finding is mitigated by this policy, and the app: origin only exists in a PACKAGED build, so no dev run could ever exercise it. Every claim for it until now was an argument about source code. First measurement in a shipped artifact.
slice47h.trap: The gate FIRST version tested enforcement with eval and reported eval-allowed, against a build whose header is demonstrably correct. Runtime.evaluate bypasses the page CSP by design, exactly as the DevTools console does, and so does Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument. Anything the harness executes directly is the wrong instrument. The gate now appends an inline <script> and listens for securitypolicyviolation: the element is created from a bypassing context but the LOAD belongs to the page. Had the first reading been recorded, the record would carry a false alarm about a live security control, pointing at a policy that was already correct.
slice47h.secondTrap: The CDP target exists as soon as the WINDOW does, before the DOCUMENT is usable - Failed to fetch and a null document.head, both of which read as findings about the policy. The gate waits for readyState complete.
slice47h.doesNotShow: The packaged artifact (built 2026-08-01) predates slice 47g extraction, so it validates the mechanism and the policy CONTENT but was built from the version with the string inline in main.ts - re-run after the next npm run package. Only script-src was exercised behaviourally; object-src, form-action, base-uri and the connect-src host list are asserted from the header text.

slice47i.title: the transitive production license tree is audited by a re-runnable gate
slice47i.scale: LICENSING_PLAN.md audited 17 declared runtime dependencies. package.json now declares 81 and the lockfile resolves 623 non-dev packages.
slice47i.finding: rvfc-polyfill (GPL-3.0) was in the shipped tree and in NO record. Fine for a GPL-3.0-or-later work; the point is that it arrived without a decision, which is what an unchecked box hides. Acknowledged now, so a THIRD unacknowledged strong-copyleft package fails the gate.
slice47i.weakCopyleftNote: 15 packages: @img/sharp-libvips-* (LGPL-3.0) and jassub, the subtitle renderer this migration adopted. LGPL to GPL-3.0 is permitted.
correctionsToLicensingPlan: Current declaration said license MIT and called it inaccurate. The ADR-001 flip HAS happened: package.json declares GPL-3.0-or-later and LICENSE is the GPLv3 text. The gate checks BOTH, because they are separate claims that have disagreed before.

Sidecar section said "unmodified pinned binary, conventional separate-program posture". NOT TRUE since slice 46 - the staged sidecar is a MODIFIED build. The plan own rule now applies: the fork source must be published on distribution, and that source is patches/seanime/*.patch plus upstream 9bdd052, which reproduce the binary exactly. The gate fails if the staged sidecar carries patch markers while patches/seanime/ is empty.
Two checklist boxes were done and unticked (license-checker over the transitive tree; replace LICENSE and set the manifest license).
gateCorrectnessNotes: The FIRST run reported jszip as unrecorded strong copyleft. Its license is (MIT OR GPL-3.0-or-later) and an OR is the LICENSEE choice - taking MIT is permitted. Only an expression whose every branch is copyleft constrains anything.
LGPL-3.0 contains the substring GPL-3.0, so weak copyleft must be tested BEFORE strong or all 15 sharp binaries read as strong copyleft.
slice47i.distribution: Nothing is distributed today (private: true), so no obligation has attached. A package built from here on ships the modified server, and that is the trigger.

slice47j.title: the packaged app survives a first run with no internet
slice47j.measured: Packaged first run on a throwaway profile with DNS blackholed: the desktop mounts, lookupTerm/lookupTermOffline/dictAvailableLangs all answer, the shell is still standing after the failures land, and the network-dependent surface degrades instead of hanging.
slice47j.differential: searchDiscovery(frieren): 6 results in 2720ms with the internet, 0 results in 1034ms with DNS blackholed. Same query, same build, only DNS changed.
slice47j.mistake: The gate FIRST version blocked requests through the RENDERER CDP Fetch domain and reported 0 blocked while searchDiscovery returned 6 real results. This app networks in the MAIN process (ipcRenderer.invoke discovery:search), and main-process requests never pass through a renderer CDP session. Only the control caught it - the gate refuses to call a run PASS unless the block bit something. Without that, "the shell survived with the internet blocked" would have been recorded about a run with the internet fully connected.
slice47j.theBlock: host-resolver-rules MAP * ~NOTFOUND, EXCLUDE localhost - applied by Chromium network stack, which Electron net module uses too. Literal 127.0.0.1 is not a hostname so the sidecar is untouched. Network.emulateNetworkConditions offline:true was rejected for the mirror-image reason: it kills loopback too and would have blamed the local server the user still has.
slice47j.doesNotShow: One surface stands in for "needs the internet". Metadata sweeps, artwork, subtitle discovery, AniList sync and Whisper first-use model download were not exercised - the last is the one most likely to behave badly offline. No media playback: this is a boot-and-surfaces run. The renderer-side witness read 0 both ways because Fetch.enable attaches after the document loads; the verdict rests on the main-process witness.

slice47l.title: an interrupted download is now actually interrupted
slice47l.test: src/main/__tests__/downloads.test.ts - "survives a connection dropped MID-TRANSFER and resumes from what it kept"
slice47l.staleChecklistItem: Phase 9 lists "interrupted-download tests". FOUR already existed (append to a partial, restart when the server ignores Range, discard a partial from another version, adopt an orphaned partial on boot), so the item was stale the same way virtualizationAtScale was. But every one of them HAND-WRITES the .part file. They cover the resume arithmetic; nothing had ever killed a transfer in flight.
slice47l.whatTheNewTestDoes: The server promises the full Content-Length, writes 800 KB of a 1.6 MB body, then destroys the socket. The app is fine: the .part and its .meta.json both survive, the retry sends Range: bytes=<what survived>-, and the reassembled file is byte-identical, which proves the running hash was rebuilt correctly across the interruption.
falseAlarms: FIRST: "the partial is discarded on a dropped connection" - measured keptBytes 0 against the existing 60 KB fixture. fs.createWriteStream buffer is 64 KB, so cutting a 60 KB transfer anywhere leaves nothing on disk: the fixture was smaller than one buffer. At real model sizes the loss is bounded by that buffer. Hence a dedicated 1.6 MB payload on its own URL.

SECOND: "it still keeps nothing at 800 KB" - also wrong. res.socket.destroy() in the same tick as res.write() throws the write away before it reaches the network; the client saw a bare fetch failed with zero bytes in 38 ms. That is the FIXTURE never sending a partial, not the app losing one. Waiting for the write callback plus a 60 ms beat produces a real mid-body abort (terminated) and the partial appears.
slice47l.lesson: Both readings looked exactly like "resume is broken". The tell in each case was the same question this track keeps having to ask: did the instrument actually do the thing it claims to have done?

slice48.theRealDefect: collectSnapshot() stores the RAW string from localStorage.getItem; writeLocal() then does setItem(key, JSON.stringify(value)) on that string. One extra JSON encoding layer per boot, unbounded. Measured: seeded at parse depth 1, read back at 2 after one completed migration, 3 after two, 4 after three, while a control key outside LS_KEYS stayed byte-identical. The app's readers parse ONCE (flashcardDeck.ts:72), so after a single migration JSON.parse(raw) returns a STRING, parsed.cards is undefined, and readStore() hands back an empty deck. The IndexedDB mirror is still correct but NOTHING restores the deck from it, and the next deck write mirrors the empty store back over the good copy.

slice48.tierDurabilityNote: Across the kill, localStorage came back SHALLOWER than it was three completed migrations earlier while IndexedDB kept everything. Chromium commits localStorage to disk lazily, so a SIGKILL can discard recent writes. The gate OBSERVES the rollback; it does not prove that mechanism.
instrumentTraps: A PROBE MUST NOT CREATE THE DATABASE. indexedDB.open('jp-study-db') with no onupgradeneeded creates an empty v1 DB with no kv object store. The app's openDb() then opens it SUCCESSFULLY - the version matches, so its upgrade handler never runs - and every withStore throws NotFoundError forever after. The migration's try/catch logs 'skipped' and does nothing, and the gate reads back byte-identical values and calls it a PASS. The first version of the gate reported THREE PASSes about a run in which the migration never executed.

SEEDING MUST NOT LAND INSIDE A RUN. runStorageMigrations reads its snapshot, awaits the IndexedDB write loop, and only THEN touches localStorage. A harness write inside that window is not in the snapshot and is REMOVED by the next line. The second version seeded right after readyState complete and reported 'all five retained keys were REMOVED' - a race in the instrument, not the app's steady-state behaviour.

THE WRITE LOOP CANNOT BE WATCHED WHILE IT RUNS. IndexedDB serialises readonly transactions behind readwrite ones on the same store, so a poll issued mid-loop does not answer until the loop has drained. Polling every 25 ms for five seconds returned 'already complete' about a loop it had been watching throughout. The kill is timed off a calibration run instead, and the proof that it landed mid-flight is read AFTERWARDS from storage-version.

A REUSED THROWAWAY PROFILE MAKES 'wait for the migration' VACUOUS. storage-version is already 5 from the previous run, so the wait returns before this boot's migration has started, the seed lands mid-run, and the depths come out three layers too deep. Fresh profile per run.

slice66.mechanism: isPluralForms (core.ts:41) only recognises an OBJECT carrying `other`. The template is returned VERBATIM, so the user reads "{count, plural, one {# result} other {# results}}" off the screen.

slice73.selfProof: All five self-proof steps passed BEFORE any number was believed. 29/29 offline assertions. The design includes NEGATIVE controls proving the check can fail (a viewport contradicting the derived scale is rejected; one stray matching pixel makes the mapping FAIL rather than skew); fiducials that are non-square and asymmetric so an x/y transposition cannot pass, in colours like (253,7,251) because a gradient can plausibly contain #ff00ff and essentially never #fd07fb; scale derived from the SEPARATION between fiducials so sub-pixel error cancels, with four independent checks that must agree or no number is produced; devicePixelRatio recorded but NOT used (evidence, not input); an anti-animation guard that reads rects, captures, then reads rects again and drops anything that moved. It states its own blind spot up front: elementFromPoint ignores pointer-events:none, which is why it reports ALONGSIDE the CSS path rather than replacing it.

The first run could not be split at all because the proof keeps only the worst 20 rows; the coordinator added belowThreeOnBothReadings / belowThreeStrictOnly to the summary. slice73.taskbarLessons: TWO things the taskbar taught. (a) THE AERO EXCLUSION RUNS DEEPER THAN THE UNDERLINE: shell.css:911 scopes the active-task ::after with :where(html:not([data-materials=aero])), and shell.css:866 scopes the "position: relative" on .os-task-win the SAME way. Adding only the ::after would have anchored it to .os-taskbar, so left:50% would centre a 16px bar on the WHOLE TASKBAR instead of the button - a visible defect the contrast metric might well have scored as fixed. Caught by asking why the dark-theme version works rather than assuming mine would. (b) THE COLOUR CHOICE INVERTS THERE: --state-indicator #00697f reads 1.17:1 on the taskbar, because this taskbar is a DARK surface inside a LIGHT theme. White is correct there. The generalisation "aero is light, so indicators go darker" breaks exactly on the taskbar.
slice73.strictMetricLimit: Even PURE WHITE fails the strict reading on the taskbar at 2.96:1, because the gradient top stop is a light blue and no flat colour clears 3:1 across the whole span. A bottom-anchored bar sits against the dark end at 10.17:1. The strict min-over-adjacent-colours reading penalises it for a colour at the opposite edge of the button; bestPairRatio is the honest reading. Written into the CSS so nobody later "fixes" a working indicator to satisfy an over-conservative number. (In the event the underline cleared BOTH readings - state went to 0.)

slice73.lastFix: The two remaining affordance failures were closed by ONE rule. A runtime probe (docs/migration/tools/probe-aero-input-border.mjs, new) dumped the computed border, outline, box-shadow, background and the RESOLVED custom properties for those elements: they resolve --border=#767380 and --control-edge=#767380 and USE NEITHER, painting rgba(104,166,196,0.95), which composites to rgb(111,170,199) and matches the sampler within antialiasing. Source: aero-apps.css:5109 targets every input/textarea/select in aero and sets border-color DIRECTLY, so a token that works by repointing --border can never reach it. Now #4f7a9b opaque (4.58:1 on white). THREE attempts to derive that colour from source were wrong; the probe settled it in one run. Printing the resolved tokens NEXT TO the painted value is what made it unambiguous - seeing #767380 sitting there unused is a far stronger statement than "the border is not what I expected".

phase9.tokensAreAdvisoryUntilProven: THE PATTERN. One brand colour cannot satisfy 1.4.11 across a dark theme and a light one at once. This track has now extracted THREE semantic tokens for jobs --accent was silently doing: --control-edge (affordance boundaries), --focus-ring-color (focus), --state-indicator (state). And in THREE separate cases a rule outranked the token meant to control it: --control-border shadowed by a later :root definition, --focus-ring-color bypassed by html[data-display-focus] *:focus-visible, --control-edge overridden by a hardcoded aero border. Tokens in this codebase are ADVISORY until something proves they win - always re-measure a token change against shipped bytes. FOURTH CASE: aero-apps.css:5109 sets border-color directly on every input in aero, bypassing --control-edge a second time.
phase9.recordingHazard: A backtick inside a node -e string is COMMAND SUBSTITUTION to bash: writing "position: relative" in backticks silently deleted that phrase from the recorded field and printed "position:: command not found". Same family as the backtick-inside-a-template-literal trap in the page-side probes. Use a quoted heredoc (<<'EOF') for anything with backticks.

slice69.security: Tokens live in the MAIN process in <userData>/mal-tokens.json, safeStorage-encrypted. The renderer is told only WHETHER an account is connected, never the token. slice70.what: Phase 8 item 2 - the secure browser/overlay host. The live <webview> guest now has study lookup; previously the Chrome extension had in-page lookup on any site while the app own browser had none (verified: repo-wide grep for ipc-message and sendToHost returned ZERO hits in src/).
slice70.latentHoleClosed: WORTH MORE THAN THE FEATURE. The <webview> relied on Electron DEFAULTS and NOTHING ENFORCED THEM - any future edit adding nodeintegration or webpreferences="contextIsolation=no" to the tag WOULD HAVE BEEN HONOURED. attachNavGuards will-attach-webview (main.ts:576) now forces nodeIntegration=false, contextIsolation=true, sandbox=true, webSecurity=true and DELETES renderer-supplied privilege attributes rather than merging them.
slice70.boundary: No new ipcMain channel exists at all - verified. The guest gets ipcRenderer.sendToHost only, which reaches the embedder element in the host renderer and NOT ipcMain, so it cannot touch the dictionary IPC. Contract is allow-list not deny-list; text <=400 chars windowed AROUND the offset; an offset that does not index its own text is a rejection not a clamp; both handlers check event.isTrusted so page script cannot forge a gesture. Rate limiting is doubled ON PURPOSE: the guest self-limits (advice, since it runs in the process being defended against) and the HOST re-limits (enforcement).
slice70.coordinatorNote: I first grepped the RENDERER for contextIsolation, found only a comment saying webpreferences was deliberately absent, and thought the claim was false. The enforcement is in MAIN, deliberately, where a compromised renderer cannot reach it. My check was in the wrong layer, not the implementation.
slice70.testFixedByCoordinator: immersionGuestBridge.test.ts asserted the serialized guest body contains WINDOW_MS = 1000 and the source says exactly that, yet it failed: the body is read back through Function.prototype.toString() AFTER esbuild transforms the module, and esbuild re-encodes the literal as 1e3. The guard was asserting how the bundler spells a number. It now parses the literal and compares numerically. 37/37.
